Empirical Research Plan  

================================================================  
1. Identification Strategy  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Method: Within-worker panel fixed-effects regression that exploits day-to-day
fluctuations in ambient ozone.  Conceptually this is a “continuous-intensity
difference-in-differences” design: each worker acts as her own control and the
only source of identifying variation is how much ozone that same worker faces
on different harvest days, net of rich time and weather controls.

Why appropriate?  
• The farm’s crews all work the same hours in the same fields, so cross-worker
variation in contemporaneous ozone is nil; identification must come from the
time dimension.  
• Photochemical formation and long-range transport make daily ozone shocks
largely orthogonal to local agricultural activities, satisfying the
(as-good-as-random) assumption once weather is controlled for.  
• A fixed-effects panel removes all time-invariant worker heterogeneity
(fatigue proneness, human capital, etc.) and crop-by-year dummies flexibly
absorb seasonality.  
• The question concerns intensive-margin productivity conditional on showing
up, exactly what the panel delivers.

Optional extension: instrument actual ozone with a “predicted ozone” measure
built from (i) up-wind monitors and (ii) same-day solar radiation interacted
with afternoon/evening wind direction.  The main plan below, however, relies on
exogeneity of day-to-day ozone conditional on weather.

================================================================  
2. Treatment and Control  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Treatment variable: Average work-day (06:00–15:00) ambient ozone concentration
in parts per billion (ppb), demeaned and measured either linearly
(preferred) or as high-ozone indicators.

Control: The same workers on lower-ozone days.

Timing: Measured contemporaneously; no discrete event date.

(If the researcher prefers a binary DID for robustness, “treated” can be
defined as days with ozone ≥ 60 ppb, well below the 75 ppb federal 8-hr
standard, vs. < 60 ppb.)

No running variable → not an RDD.

================================================================  
3. Key Identifying Assumptions  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
A1. Conditional exogeneity: After controlling for temperature, humidity,
pressure, wind, crop-by-year fixed effects, day-of-week fixed effects and
year-specific trends, the remaining variation in ozone is as good as random
with respect to workers’ unobserved productivity shocks.  
Plausible because ozone is produced off-site and transported long distances.

A2. No worker-specific shocks perfectly collinear with ozone: e.g. an individual
getting sick only on high-ozone days.  Worker FE eliminate time-invariant
health, and the short 2-season horizon limits systematic intra-worker patterns.

A3. No interference (SUTVA): A worker’s output responds only to the ozone she
breathes, not to a co-worker’s ozone.  Holds because the exposure is common
across the farm.

A4. Stable composition: The set of workers present on a given harvest day is
not systematically selected by ozone.  Plausible since crews are assembled
before sunrise with minimal information on same-day ozone; nevertheless we test
for ozone effects on attendance.

================================================================  
4. Main Threats & Mitigation  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
T1. Weather confounding (temperature, humidity, solar radiation)  
 • Mitigation: Control flexibly for weather
  ‒ Include cubic temperature, cubic dew point, precipitation, wind speed.  
  ‒ Interact temperature bins with crop-by-year FE.  
 • Robustness: Estimate with and without each weather block to show stability.

T2. Seasonality/crop growth stages correlated with ozone  
 • Mitigation: Include crop × year × harvest-week fixed effects or
day-of-season splines; this absorbs any smooth seasonal productivity trend.  

T3. Endogenous labor supply/intensive margin mixing  
 • Mitigation: Use output per hour (pieces/hour) as the dependent variable
thus netting out changes in hours; additionally, estimate a first-stage probit
for “worker present” to show ozone does not affect attendance.

Optional IV threat (if IV used): Relevance and exclusion of wind-based
instruments—check Kleibergen-Paap F-stat and run over-identification tests.

================================================================  
5. R Code Outline  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
```r
# -------------------------------------------
# 0.  Packages
# -------------------------------------------
library(data.table)
library(fixest)      # fast high-dimensional FE
library(lmtest)      # coeftest, waldtest
library(sandwich)    # robust vcov

# -------------------------------------------
# 1.  Data loading
# -------------------------------------------
# assume two CSVs: payroll.csv, airmeteo.csv
pay  <- fread("payroll.csv")      # worker-day panel
air  <- fread("airmeteo.csv")     # monitor-day data

# -------------------------------------------
# 2.  Merge & variable construction
# -------------------------------------------
setDT(pay); setDT(air)
air[, date := as.IDate(date)]
pay[, date := as.IDate(date)]

# merge nearest monitor (already averaged 06–15h)
dat <- merge(pay, air, by = c("date"), all.x = TRUE)

# Productivity measure
dat[, pieces_per_hr := pieces / hours_worked]

# Ozone in 10-ppb units for easier interpretation
dat[, ozone10 := ozone_ppb / 10]

# Weather controls (polynomials)
dat[, `:=`(temp  = temp_c,
           temp2 = temp_c^2,
           temp3 = temp_c^3,
           rhum  = rel_humidity,
           rhum2 = rel_humidity^2)]

# Fixed-effect identifiers
dat[, worker_id := factor(worker_id)]
dat[, crop_year  := interaction(crop, year)]
dat[, dow        := weekdays(date)]
dat[, harvest_wk := as.integer(format(date, "%V"))]   # ISO week of year

# -------------------------------------------
# 3.  Main specification
# -------------------------------------------
fe_formula <- "pieces_per_hr ~ ozone10 + temp + temp2 + temp3 +
                             rhum + rhum2 + wind_speed +
                             solar_radiation | 
                             worker_id + crop_year:harvest_wk + dow"

main_mod <- feols(as.formula(fe_formula),
                  data = dat,
                  cluster = ~date)   # cluster at day level

summary(main_mod)

# -------------------------------------------
# 4.  Robustness check 1:  binary treatment
# -------------------------------------------
dat[, high_ozone := (ozone_ppb >= 60)]
rb_mod <- feols(pieces_per_hr ~ high_ozone + temp + temp2 + temp3 +
                                   rhum + rhum2 + wind_speed +
                                   solar_radiation |
                                   worker_id + crop_year:harvest_wk + dow,
                data = dat,
                cluster = ~date)
summary(rb_mod)

# -------------------------------------------
# 5.  Robustness check 2:  Leads & lags placebo
# -------------------------------------------
dat[, ozone10_lag1 := shift(ozone10,  1L, type = "lag"), by = date]
dat[, ozone10_lead1:= shift(ozone10,  1L, type = "lead"),by = date]

placebo_mod <- feols(pieces_per_hr ~ ozone10 + ozone10_lead1 +
                                        ozone10_lag1 + 
                                        temp + temp2 + temp3 +
                                        rhum + rhum2 + wind_speed +
                                        solar_radiation |
                                        worker_id + crop_year:harvest_wk + dow,
                     data = dat,
                     cluster = ~date)
summary(placebo_mod)
```
The code:
(1) loads data,  
(2) constructs productivity and ozone variables,  
(3) runs the high-dimensional fixed-effects model with day-level clustering,  
(4) repeats with a binary “high ozone” DID, and  
(5) adds one-day leads to test for pre-trends (coefficients on leads should be
≈ 0).

================================================================  
6. Expected Results  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
Sign of β (ozone) – negative.  Medical evidence links ozone to acute
respiratory irritation, so each 10 ppb increase is predicted to lower physical
work output.  Magnitude: back-of-the-envelope elasticity around −0.02 to
−0.04, i.e., a 10 ppb rise (roughly an inter-quartile shift in the Central
Valley) reduces pieces harvested per hour by 2–4 percent.

================================================================  
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment  
----------------------------------------------------------------  
(Scale: 1 = clearly satisfied, 0 = questionable)

C1. Treatment exogeneity conditional on controls …… 0.8 (≈1)  
C2. No interference/SUTVA ………………………………………… 1  
C3. No differential attrition or selection ……………… 0.7  
C4. Correct functional form / sufficient controls …… 0.8  
C5. Inference: proper clustering and serial corr. …… 1  

Overall ≈ 4.3 / 5.
